title: tarasque
description:
make a lore video on the tarasque from dnd.
start with a narrative on a civilian's perspective living in a village near where the tarasque wakes up
continue with a description of what makes it so powerful 
conclude with a description of how the tarasque can be 'defeated'

script.draft:
Here is the full script:

---

# 🐉 TARRASQUE — Full YouTube Script

---

[VISUAL: ground-level shot of a medieval village at dusk, thatched-roof cottages, a dirt road running through the center, warm lantern light in windows, mud and straw on the ground, slight camera shake as dust and small pebbles begin to vibrate on the road surface]

The ground shakes. Just a little. Like something enormous turned over in its sleep. The farmers feel it. The innkeeper feels it. The children feel it through the soles of their bare feet. Nobody in this village has seen it before. But every grandmother, every travelling merchant, every half-drunk soldier at the bar knows exactly what that rumble means.

The Tarrasque is waking up.

There is only one of them. It sleeps somewhere deep within the world's core, and no one — no wizard, no oracle, no god — can predict when it will rise again. When it does, the only warning you get is the ground telling you so.

---

[VISUAL: massive creature bursting upward through cracked earth in an open field, viewed from below at a steep upward angle, daylight behind it, silhouette of the Tarrasque — a broad quadruped with two large forward-facing horns, spines along its back, a thick armored carapace, and a heavy sweeping tail, dust and rock fragments raining down]

The beast stands 50 feet tall and stretches 70 feet long — a quadruped with a long tail, reflective carapace, and two great horns jutting from its head. Its purpose is literally to eat the world. Whenever it wakes from its slumber, the Tarrasque wanders the Material Plane consuming anything in its path — mountains, kingdoms, people, monsters. None are safe from its endless hunger.

And it is nearly impossible to stop. The Tarrasque cannot be frightened or charmed, and has resistances to every kind of damage imaginable. It has Legendary Resistance — meaning if it fails a saving throw, it simply chooses to succeed instead. Point a spell at it? Its Reflective Carapace means ranged spells may simply bounce off — and on a bad roll, that spell fires straight back at the caster. It also carries the Siege Monster trait, dealing double damage to every structure and object it touches. Walls mean nothing. Fortresses mean nothing. Entire cities are just a meal.

In 5th edition, the Tarrasque holds one of only two Challenge Rating 30 slots in the entire game — the other being Tiamat herself.

---

[VISUAL: a small party of four adventurers — a warrior in heavy plate armor, a robed wizard with a glowing staff, a hooded ranger, and a cleric in white vestments — standing on a hilltop at dawn looking down at the Tarrasque in a valley below, wide establishing shot, early morning mist, the creature's silhouette dwarfing the landscape]

So how do you stop it? The honest answer: you probably don't kill it. You survive it. In older editions, the Tarrasque regenerated from literally anything — even a disintegrate spell couldn't put it down for good, and permanently killing it required a Wish spell to seal the deal. Modern rules stripped the regeneration, but the fight remains a last resort for the most powerful adventurers alive.

The Tarrasque exists only to eat, kill, and destroy. It has the intelligence of an animal and cannot speak. It is neutrally aligned — its savagery isn't evil, because it simply lacks the mind to choose. That actually matters. In the original French legend that inspired it, Saint Martha stopped the beast not with weapons, but with hymns and prayers — charming it, then leading it back to the town of Tarascon, where the citizens finished the job.

That's the secret the legend whispers: you don't out-muscle the Tarrasque. You out-think it. Lure it. Trap it. Banish it. Put it back to sleep and pray the ground stays quiet for another thousand years.

Because the Tarrasque doesn't stop. It doesn't negotiate. It doesn't retreat.

It just *eats*.

---

[VISUAL: aerial wide shot of a ruined village — collapsed stone walls, scorched earth, a single broken cart wheel in the foreground, no people, an eerie stillness, golden hour lighting casting long shadows across the rubble, camera slowly pulling back to reveal the full scale of destruction stretching to the horizon]

Few things survive a Tarrasque's rampage, and reports of its devastation are often contradictory, incomplete, or beyond belief. In cases where it leaves no survivors, its calamities are sometimes blamed on evil dragons or magical disasters.

But those who know? They recognize the silence it leaves behind.

If you want more deep dives into D&D's most legendary monsters — hit subscribe. The next one might just be worse.
